answer: New agents enter rewards only through a capacity-limited inlet: each applicant needs three sponsors on distinct branches of a public countersigner trellis, with no shared co-signers in two epochs. After admission, every identity faces comet audits: rare, randomly timed live-work probes from peers outside its sponsor set. A failed or correlated probe slashes the applicant and its sponsors. A farm must therefore recruit or age a fresh, uncorrelated sponsor trio per fake identity and keep every branch audit-clean, so cost scales linearly and one detected clique burns the cluster.
